about.title: Davis Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Davis residents rely on everyday products at home, on campus, and while commuting along corridors like I-80, 5th Street, Russell Boulevard, and Mace Boulevard — from vehicle components and bicycle parts to household appliances and tools. When a product fails because of a flawed design, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, the people who get hurt often face medical bills and questions about who's responsible. California law allows injured people to pursue claims against manufacturers, distributors, and retailers without necessarily proving negligence. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle claims directly; instead, we connect Davis residents with independent attorneys who evaluate defective product cases and explain options in plain language. If a product injured you or someone in your household, it helps to preserve the item exactly as it was at the time of the incident, since it may serve as evidence. Reaching out for a free case review costs nothing and carries no obligation.
commonInjuries: Burns from malfunctioning appliances or electronics
Lacerations or amputations from faulty tools or machinery
Head or brain injuries from failed safety equipment
Broken bones from collapsing furniture or structures
Poisoning or illness from contaminated goods
Crush injuries from defective vehicle or bicycle parts

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Defective Product

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California generally applies strict liability to defective products, meaning you may not have to prove the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and caused harm.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may broaden the paths available for pursuing a claim.

items.title: The Product Itself Is Key Evidence
items.desc: Because design, manufacturing, and warning defects are proven through the product, an attorney can advise on preserving it properly before it's lost, repaired, or discarded.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability approach to defective products generally focuses on whether the product itself was defective and caused your injury, rather than requiring proof of carelessness. An independent attorney can review your situation to see how this applies.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, including packaging, instructions, or parts. Avoid repairing or discarding it, since it may be important evidence in evaluating your claim.

items.question: I live near I-80 or Mace Boulevard — does that matter for a product claim?
items.answer: Location itself doesn't change product liability law, but if the defect involved a vehicle part or equipment used while traveling those Davis corridors, details about where and how the incident happened can still help an attorney understand your case.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
